Paper Title: Combining Fiber Bragg Grating and Artificial Intelligence Technologies for Supporting Epidural Procedures
Keywords: AI, epidural puncture, FBG, force sensing, LOR, support vector machine
Objective: To support epidural procedures by enhancing LOR detection using AI-driven identification based on FBG data.
Methodology: FBG flexible cap + SVM trained using Leave-One-Out strategy on 10 subjects.
Results: 99.23% overall accuracy in identifying LOR events while maintaining minimal false positives.

Paper Title: Spinal Column Needle With a Force Feedback: Introductory Study
Keywords: embedded sensors, back pain, tactile feedback, sensing needle
Objective: Develop a device capable of sensing the touching point and returning a signal indicating pressing force magnitude.
Methodology: Load cell (FX1901-111N) + Arduino Uno + LED/LCD visual indicators on 3D printed handle.
Results: Force feedback correctly indicated distinct tissue types in a lumbar spine model.

Paper Title: Design and Validation of a High-Sensitivity FBG-Based Triaxial Force Sensor With Serially Configured Flexures for Percutaneous Puncture
Keywords: Fiber Bragg grating (FBG), percutaneous puncture, triaxial force sensor
Objective: Design a high-sensitivity triaxial force sensor with low-coupling for robotic puncture surgery.
Methodology: Serially configured axial/radial flexures with suspended FBG + BPNN nonlinear decoupling algorithm.
Results: Resolutions of 2.6 mN (axial) and 0.25 mN (radial) with crosstalk limited to 4.36%.

Paper Title: Testing Effectiveness of a Teaching Tool That Uses a Non-Contact Sensor for Preventing Lower Back Pain
Keywords: non-contact sensor, self-training, low back pain prevention, nursing students
Objective: Test effectiveness of non-contact sensors to raise awareness of postures that prevent lower back pain.
Methodology: Xtion infrared camera + sound alerts for dangerous angles (30 degrees) during bedmaking tasks.
Results: 70% of users improved base support area and center of gravity control; effective for posture awareness.

Paper Title: CNN-Based Methods for Object Recognition With High-Resolution Tactile Sensors
Keywords: Tactile sensors, object recognition, deep learning, deep CNN
Objective: Identify contacted objects using high-resolution pressure-sensor arrays as images.
Methodology: Comparison of transfer learning (VGG16/AlexNet) vs custom-made 'TactNet' trained on tactile images.
Results: TactNet achieved over 93% accuracy with significantly lower computational load for embedded systems.

Paper Title: Assessing the Risk of Low Back Pain and Injury via Inertial and Barometric Sensors
Keywords: Activity recognition, AI, smart clothes, wearable sensors, risk assessment
Objective: Assess safety level of workers lifting loads using unobtrusive wearable sensors.
Methodology: Reflective safety jacket + barometric altimeters + IMU + neural classifier (MLP).
Results: 95.6% classification accuracy in detecting safe vs unsafe lifting behaviors across 30 subjects.

Paper Title: A Pain Intensity Assessment Method Based on High-Density Flexible Tactile Sensor Array
Keywords: Cross-section of pulse wave, Sensor array, Pain perception, high-density flexible sensor
Objective: Assess pain by monitoring radial artery transverse instability revealed in 3D pulse waveforms.
Methodology: 18 MEMS pressure sensors on polyimide FPC + cubic spline interpolation + sub-pixel algorithms.
Results: Recognition error of only 0.0368 mm in tracking periodic migration (CTP) of the pulse barycenter.

Paper Title: Development and Performance Evaluation of an Optical Tactile Sensor Using Transparent Flexible Resin
Keywords: Tactile sensor, Force sensor, Optical device, Transparent polymer
Objective: Develop an inexpensive optical tactile sensor reproducing the functions and flexibility of human hands.
Methodology: Transparent polyurethane resin block + photo-reflector elements + polynomial approximation for 3-axis force.
Results: Resolution < 0.1 mm, durability confirmed over 20,000 presses, and cost < 5,000 yen.

Paper Title: Foldable Forceps with Tactile Sensor Array for Tissue Identification and Suture Needle Status Detection for Surgical Robot
Keywords: foldable forceps, piezoresistive effect, surgical robot, tissue identification
Objective: Create foldable tactile forceps for tissue palpation and needle tracking in MIS.
Methodology: Foldable linkage + 4x8 monopolar piezoresistive array + CD4051 multiplexer for data acquisition.
Results: Verified ability to localize suture needles and detect large lumps via simulation and single-point testing.

Paper Title: Total Force Analysis and Safety Enhancing for Operating Both Guidewire and Catheter in Endovascular Surgery
Keywords: Total force analysis, safety enhancing, guidewire and catheter, haptic force feedback
Objective: Improve VIS safety by analyzing total forces and confirming tip collision using a new force sensor.
Methodology: Force modeling + Master-Slave haptic system + pressure-sensitive rubber based sensor (2.7mm OD).
Results: Successful detection of catheter-to-wall collisions; haptic feedback accuracy enhanced by force decoupling.

Paper Title: Multifingered Object Recognition with Tactile Sensors and Graph Convolutional Networks using Topological Graph Segmentation
Keywords: GCNs, Allegro Hand, uSkin, object recognition, topological segmentation
Objective: Investigate if hand graph segmentation simplifies processing and improves tactile recognition.
Methodology: Comparing Full Hand GCN vs Digits vs Patch-based GCNs on an Allegro Hand with 384 taxels.
Results: Patch-level segmentation yielded 92.92% accuracy and used 50% less GPU memory than the baseline.

Paper Title: Object Recognition for Humanoid Robots Using Full Hand Tactile Sensor
Keywords: Electronic skin, robot hand, tactile recognition, InceptionNetV3
Objective: Develop an object learning and recognition system for humanoid robots using artificial electronic skin.
Methodology: 15 sensor arrays (551 pixels) + InceptionNetV3 (transfer learning) vs BoW models.
Results: Highest accuracy of 98.28% from only one capture using InceptionNetV3; outperforms BoW models.

Paper Title: Object Recognition Using Glove Tactile Sensor
Keywords: tactile object recognition, glove tactile sensor, BoW, CNN
Objective: Compare recognition performance using a tactile glove for humanoid robots.
Methodology: Comparison of SIFT-based Bag of Words (BoW) + KNN vs CNN (AlexNet).
Results: CNN accuracy of 97.20% significantly outperformed BoW (70.80%).

Paper Title: MiniTac: An Ultra-Compact Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for Enhanced Palpation in Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
Keywords: RAMIS, miniature tactile sensor, tumor detection, vision-based tactile sensor
Objective: Design a vision-based sensor compact enough (8mm OD) for standard surgical ports.
Methodology: Mechanoresponsive photonic elastomer + miniature camera + SVM classifier on surface deformation mean/std.
Results: Achieved 100% accuracy in detecting tumors at depths of 1-7 mm in ex-vivo porcine liver.

Paper Title: Tactile Sensors for Minimally Invasive Surgery: A Review of the State-of-the-Art, Applications, and Perspectives
Keywords: MIS, RMIS, tactile sensors, piezoelectric, optical sensors, capacitive
Objective: Map the state-of-the-art tactile sensors for MIS applications including biopsy, ablation, and valvuloplasty.
Methodology: Systematic literature review (2000-2019) on electrical and optical sensing principles.
Results: Identified miniaturization and MRI/electrical passivity as key future research directions.

Paper Title: Tactile Sensor-Based Estimation of Grasp Force and Contact State With Soft Fingers
Keywords: Force and tactile sensing, grasping, soft sensors, regression
Objective: Estimate total force exerted by soft fingers to identify contact states like stick or slip.
Methodology: Silicone fingers + dielectric elastomer sensors + GRU neural network for force regression.
Results: Model robust to object geometry changes; force error of ~16% in fixed grasp conditions.

Paper Title: A High-Sensitivity Tactile Sensor Array Based on Fiber Bragg Grating Sensing for Tissue Palpation in Minimally Invasive Surgery
Keywords: FBG, MIS, tactile sensor, tissue palpation, tumor detection
Objective: Develop a high-sensitivity FBG sensor array for localizing tissue abnormalities.
Methodology: Five tactile cells with spiral elastomers and suspended FBGs to avoid chirping.
Results: Resolution up to 0.93 mN; successfully localized tumors embedded 8 mm deep in silicone phantoms.

Paper Title: A Piezoelectric Tactile Sensor and Human-inspired Tactile Exploration Strategy for Lump Palpation
Keywords: Piezoelectric, lump palpation, human-inspired exploration, simultaneous actuation and sensing
Objective: Combine sensor development with tactile exploration strategies for lump localization.
Methodology: PZT patch on spiral steel beam + vibrotactile feedback + 'Scanning' vs 'Edge following' strategies.
Results: 'Scanning' provides highest accuracy in localization, while 'Edge following' is most efficient for shape.

Paper Title: Texture-based Intraoperative Image Guidance for Tumor Localization in Minimally Invasive Surgery
Keywords: Ultrasound, GLCM, k-means, HMM, tumor localization
Objective: Develop image guidance that classifies tactile-guided ultrasound texture regions.
Methodology: 1D k-means clustering of GLCM features + HMM-based belief propagation on sequential US images.
Results: Localized tumors in ex-vivo tissue with 98% accuracy, 99% sensitivity, and 97% specificity.

Paper Title: Miniaturized Optical Force Sensor for Minimally Invasive Surgery With Learning-Based Nonlinear Calibration
Keywords: Force sensor, MIS, optical sensor, LIM, machine learning, SVR
Objective: Develop a miniaturized VBR LIM-based force sensor for 1-DOF grasping force measurements.
Methodology: 3D printed flexible shell + optical fiber + SVR calibration with relative voltage/rate features.
Results: Accuracy (MAE) of 0.12 N, resolution of 0.002 N, and repeatability of 0.07 N achieved.

Paper Title: Grasping-Force-Based Passive Safety Method for a Vascular Interventional Surgery Robot System
Keywords: Passive safety, robot-assisted surgery, VIS robot, friction coupling
Objective: Improve VIS safety using a passive friction-based method to cutoff excessive inserting forces.
Methodology: SEA-based guidewire manipulator + orthogonal force coupling model based on molecular friction.
Results: Reduced contact force by ~40% in front/middle sections; automatic grasping force adjustment ensured safety.

Paper Title: Design and Application of Optical Fiber Sensors for Force Myography
Keywords: force myography, optical fiber sensors, gesture recognition
Objective: Evaluate optical fiber transducers for assessing radial forces of forearm muscles for FMG.
Methodology: Microbending transducer + visible light LED + CCD camera + ANN classifier for 4 postures.
Results: Successful real-time control of a virtual prosthetic hand with ~99.7% posture identification accuracy.

Paper Title: Wavelength-Phase Hybrid Coded Catheter Tip Three-Axis Force Optical Fiber Sensor
Keywords: FBG, 3-axis force sensor, error compensation, fault-tolerant decoupling
Objective: Measure CF during RFCA with tolerance for FBG fracture and environmental interference.
Methodology: Wavelength-phase hybrid coding (FBG + F-P cavity) + SHO-BPNN fault-tolerant algorithm.
Results: Full-scale relative errors < 6% during fault states; compensation effectively handled pressure/temperature errors.

Paper Title: Plastic Optical Fiber Sensor for Handgrip Force Monitoring During Physical Rehabilitation
Keywords: handgrip force, physical rehabilitation, POF sensor, macrobending
Objective: Monitor handgrip force for breast cancer survivors using low-cost POF sensors.
Methodology: POF attached to handspring tool + LED + photodiode measuring macrobending power loss.
Results: Sensitivity of -7 mV/N; effectively distinguished movement patterns and maximum effort between subjects.

Paper Title: Smart Cutting Tool Integrated With Optical Fiber Sensors for Cutting Force Measurement
Keywords: Cutting force, optical fiber sensors, smart cutting tool
Objective: Measure real-time cutting forces in harsh industrial environments using FBG sensors.
Methodology: FBG sensors bonded to tool shank surfaces to measure bending strains in three directions.
Results: Good agreement with Kistler dynamometer; FBG sensors provided EMI immunity and long-distance transmission.

Paper Title: Haptic Feedback Based Laparoscope Movement Perception Method
Keywords: Robotic surgery, haptic feedback, instrument tracking, virtual fixtures
Objective: Enhance surgeon control over laparoscopic view during autonomous instrument tracking.
Methodology: Sigma.7 master device providing repulsive force (FRVF) based on instrument-to-image center distance.
Results: Effectively informed surgeons of movement direction, improving situational awareness without holding the scope.

Paper Title: Image-based Pose Estimation and Tracking of Surgical Instruments in Minimally Invasive Surgery
Keywords: object pose estimation, surgical instrument tracking, stereo vision, Kalman filter
Objective: Propose an image-based pose estimation system for MIS training and autonomous operations.
Methodology: Color markers + stereo camera (SGBM) + Kalman filter + kinematic angle calculation algorithm.
Results: Endpoint absolute error < 2.7 mm, joint angle MAE < 0.11 rad; suitable for surgery training.

Paper Title: A Compact FBG-Based Triaxial Force Sensor With Parallel Helical Beams
Keywords: FBG, force sensor, parallel helical beams, robotic-assisted surgery
Objective: Realize surgical palpation and safety via a compact triaxial FBG force sensor.
Methodology: Parallel helical beams for balanced stiffness + 4 FBG fibers distributed circularly.
Results: Resolutions of 0.01 N (axial) and 0.012 N (radial) in a 0-5 N range; successfully recognized material stiffness.

Paper Title: Flexible Tactile-Sensing Gripper Design and Excessive Force Protection Function
Keywords: Medical robots, soft sensors, tactile sensing, excessive force protection
Objective: Realize stable catheter grasping and tactile sensing with an excessive force protection function (EFPF).
Methodology: FTG made of natural rubber + Vision-based marking point tracking + EFPF shrinking algorithm.
Results: Average force error ~37 mN; EFPF maintained catheter force below 393 mN in carotid tests.

Paper Title: Grasping Force Control of Robotic Gripper With High Stiffness
Keywords: Force feedback, grasping, hysteresis, ADRC, backlash compensation
Objective: Control grasping force for Smart-Touch inspection in high-stiffness rigid grippers.
Methodology: Hybrid controller integrating Preisach-operator backlash inversion + ADRC with Extended State Observer (ESO).
Results: ADRC reduced steady-state error by 73% and overshoot by 62% compared to standard PI control.
